By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in S.T.No.146 of 2023, Case Crime No.402 of 2023 at Police Station-Kurra, District-Mainpuri under Sections 363,
366, 376(3) IPC and Sections 3/4(2) of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in jail since 24.09.2023.

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 09.02.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Ram Badan Maurya, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Akhilesh Bharti, learned counsel for the informant and Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 17 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no lawful basis for the age related entry of the victim in the school records.
The school records disclosing her age as 15 years and 6 months are unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 18 years of age and 17 years 5 months of age respectively.
(iv) Medico-legal examination (not the age determination test) records that the victim is about 17 years of age.

(v) No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as it would establish the majority of the victim and falsify the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.

3. The incident occurred on 05.09.2023 and the F.I.R. was got registered on 07.09.2023.
4. Delay of two days in lodgement of the F.I.R. in the facts of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.
5. The victim and the applicant were intimate.
6. The victim and the applicant were intimate and had a consensual physical relationship.

sentences.text: 7. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship with the applicant.
8. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant.
She has also asserted that she eloped with the applicant to Etawah and thereafter went to New Delhi.
She rode pillion on motorcycle being driven by the applicant.
She resided with the applicant for one day and one night.

9. False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim against the applicant in the latter part of her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents only to save the failing prosecution case.
10. The victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. too has admitted to a romantic relationship with the applicant.
She has also asserted that she called the applicant to her house and eloped with him.
The couple first went to Etawah and thereafter to New Delhi by train.
Lastly she has stated that she has physical consensual relations with the applicant.

11. The applicant has not made any allegation of commission of rape, abduction or forceful assault in the statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. or 164 Cr.P.C.
12.
The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at public places.
She did not raise an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
Her conduct shows that she was a consenting party.
13. Major inconsistencies in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C., as well as the recitals in the F.I.R. discredit the prosecution case.
14. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
15. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
16. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Aman be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
